column2: Settings > Game: display, comfort, light and shadows, player names (distance, or hidden); the Image tab for the rest. One-click presets; in game: F10 menu.
One page, seven tabs: Game, Image, Sound & voice, Co-op (your lobbies, the network, the port), Keys, Theme, Launcher (language, updates, game folder, troubleshooting).
Preset, Display, Comfort & in-game display, and the Light & shadows summary; everything else is in the Image tab. Unity's configuration window is now skipped: set your screen here.
Vanilla brings the game back as it is, without MWCoop's additions; Ultra turns everything up to the max. Every row stays editable: the pill then moves to Custom.
SETTINGS — Game, Co-op and Mods. Game and Co-op open the same Settings page, with its tabs (Game, Image, Sound & voice, Co-op, Keys, Theme, Launcher) and its \"Search a setting…\" field.
Image: the whole picture (HDR, bloom, contrast, sun shafts, lamp coronas, headlight range) and the shadows (sun, moon, houses, distance, detail, headlights, street lights).

The Preset card of the Game tab sets everything at once: Vanilla (the game as is, without MWCoop's additions), Light (old PC), Balanced, Pretty (shadows, HDR), Ultra (everything max). As soon as you change a row, the pill moves to Custom. Just for you: the others see no difference; in game, the F10 menu has the same settings.

Image > Image and Shadows: HDR, bloom, contrast, sun shafts, GTA-style coronas, headlight range; sun, moon and house shadows, shadow distance and detail, headlight and street light shadows. The \"medium\" and \"heavy\" tags say what each row costs.
Ray tracing: set aside for now, it will come back later. The game's light and shadows stay adjustable in the Image tab.
